proposed_from.topic: Joint-polytope randomized minimax-regret treatment rules under categorical-IV partial identification. For finite positive-probability covariate strata, finite randomized Z, categorical A, and binary Y under exclusion and response-type exogeneity, construct each full response-function action-mean polytope; derive observable dual inequalities iff a pure rule is minimax, enumerate the entire optimal-mixture correspondence, and specialize to Stoye's spike-state result when all spikes are feasible. Build a Bonferroni Clopper-Pearson simultaneous multinomial fiber, cover the population optimizer correspondence, and certify deployed worst-case regret with unique-face root-n theory and uniform set-valued validity across face intersections. Include the exact three-action witness with mu0<=mu2, joint rule q=(0,1/4,3/4), value 3/16, and rectangle rule q=(0,0,1), value 1/4, and target Hruza et al.'s released multicategory implementation. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Exact response-type enumeration for the supplied three-action categorical-IV law attained all ten projected vertices and confirmed the nonrectangular constraint mu0<=mu2. The induced joint-polytope minimax rule q=(0,1/4,3/4) has regret 3/16, while actionwise rectangularization gives q=(0,0,1) and regret 1/4. Writing the response fiber as W(p)={w>=0:Bw=p} reduces the general problem to a finite primal-dual basis enumeration. On the simultaneous Clopper-Pearson event, unioning optimizer correspondences over the confidence fiber contains the true population correspondence, and robust optimization over that fiber upper-bounds deployed regret. Checks covered zero-probability observed cells, every claimed vertex, face ties, rare-cell vacuity, and the Stoye/Hruza/general robust-decision collisions; only the LP machinery was generic. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove Hadamard differentiability of the parametric LP optimizer and value maps on an explicit nondegenerate unique-face margin class, yielding the claimed root-n normal policy and regret law while retaining set-valued uniform validity at face intersections. EARLY KILL TEST: Exhaustively enumerate active bases for the twenty-type witness and its codimension-one face-boundary perturbations, compare every pure-rule certificate and optimizer union with independent exact LP solutions, and stop if any optimizer is omitted or any certificate is false.
proposed_from.novelty_justification: The theorem-level delta is the observable moving-coefficient KKT result: uniform response-basis and active-face stability, the explicit derivative \(-E H^{-1}(DH)u\), a projective-normal obstruction to a fixed-matrix right-hand-side representation, and a uniform asymptotic linear and Gaussian law for the population mixed policy and regret. The response-polytope saddle composition is background; the pure-rule, rectangle-frontier, exact witness, and finite-sample coverage results support the inference kernel.

proposed_from.literature_map: Hruza et al. (2026, Sections 2--3 and Discussion) define deterministic categorical rules and an interval loss, prove a surrogate excess-risk inequality, release multicategory code, and explicitly defer randomized rules. Song et al. (2026, Theorem 1 and its Strassen-coupling sufficiency proof) give a sharp full counterfactual compatibility characterization and simultaneous inference for linear functionals, but no decision correspondence. Stoye (2007, Proposition 1 and Examples 1--2) solves the many-treatment allocation problem under feasible spike states and shows that a pure minimax rule can be unique. Sachs et al. (2023) provide the finite response-function primal--dual template; Mastin, Jaillet, and Chin (2014) provide the finite randomized-regret game template. Klatt, Munk, and Zemel (2022) and Liu, Bunea, and Niles-Weed (2023) derive optimizer limits and confidence sets for fixed-matrix, random-right-hand-side linear programs, leaving moving saddle coefficients untreated. Bonnans and Shapiro (2000) identify the active-system rank and complementarity ingredients for sensitivity. Fang and Santos (2019) delimit full versus directional differentiability and derivative-aware resampling. Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer (2007) make the set-valued target explicit; Clopper and Pearson (1934) provide the exact cellwise inversion. Montiel Olea, Qiu, and Stoye (2026) analyze a different local Gaussian treatment-choice experiment rather than the fixed-law categorical-instrument optimizer map. No closer paper found in searches for randomized categorical-instrument minimax regret, joint-polytope treatment rules, or coefficient-varying optimizer-correspondence inference subsumes the selected kernel.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem 1 — thm:unique-face-rootn
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The Gaussian and Hadamard-differentiability claims are conditional on the observable fixed-support, response-basis, active-face, rank, slack, and complementarity margins defining P_{kappa,epsilon}; face intersections are excluded.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The moving-coefficient uniform asymptotic law holds on P_{kappa,epsilon}, not at arbitrary categorical-IV laws or optimal-face intersections.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Open-ended Question 1 — oeq:face-intersection-contraction
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The proposal does not assume a directional-inference solution at face intersections; it supplies an explicit adjacent-basis/Fang--Santos handle as the unresolved construction route.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Finite-sample correspondence coverage remains claimed at ties, while uniform contracting root-n inference at intersections remains open.

banked_reason: The promised Hruza-implementation comparison has been replaced by a generic randomized rectangle-oracle separation: the theorem does not establish that Hruza et al.'s deterministic learned rule has this oracle.
